name: Aachen Cathedral
description: Royal chapel founded by Charlemagne, coronation church of German kings for over 600 years.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1978); greatest Carolingian monument; burial place of Charlemagne.
architectural_features: Octagonal dome with Carolingian mosaics, Palatine Chapel interior, Gothic choir added 1355, imperial throne, Treasury with Reliquary of the Virgin.

name: Abu Simbel Temples
description: Two massive rock-cut temples built by Ramesses II, moved in 1968 during the Aswan High Dam rescue operation.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); greatest feat of archaeological relocation in history; aligned so sun illuminates inner sanctuary twice yearly.
architectural_features: Four 20-metre colossi of Ramesses II at facade, 36m-high entrance, four sanctuary statues, smaller Temple of Hathor with six columned statues of Nefertari.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Nubian Monuments

name: Acropolis of Athens
description: Ancient citadel located on a rocky outcrop above Athens, containing the remains of several historically significant buildings.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); symbol of ancient Greek democracy and civilization.
architectural_features: Propylaea monumental entrance, Temple of Athena Nike, Erechtheion with Caryatid porch, Parthenon, ancient fortification walls, theater of Dionysus below.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Acropolis of Athens

name: Ajanta Caves
description: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist cave monuments in a horseshoe-shaped gorge, famous for ancient wall paintings and sculptures.
historical_significance: Masterpieces of Buddhist art; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); represents over two centuries of Indian painting tradition.
architectural_features: Rock-cut viharas (monasteries) and chaityas (prayer halls), vivid Jataka tale frescoes, sculpted Buddhas and bodhisattvas, carved wooden doors, horseshoe-shaped facade on Chaitya caves.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Ajanta Caves

name: Aksum (Axum)
description: Ancient city and capital of the Kingdom of Aksum, one of the great civilizations of the ancient world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1980); legendary resting place of the Ark of the Covenant; birthplace of Ethiopian civilization.
architectural_features: 24m obelisk (stelae) with false doors and windows, King Ezana's inscription, ruins of royal palaces, underground tombs, Church of St. Mary of Zion.

name: Alcatraz Island
description: Island prison in San Francisco Bay, once housing infamous criminals like Al Capone.
historical_significance: National Heritage Site; symbol of untouchable security; now a popular museum of American criminal history.
architectural_features: Main penitentiary building with cellblocks, hospital wing, warden's house, execution chamber, radar and searchlight platforms, prison farm ruins.

name: Alhambra Palace
description: Stunning palace and fortress complex showcasing the finest Islamic architecture in Western Europe.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984); last great monument of Islamic Spain; masterpiece of Nasrid architecture.
architectural_features: Court of the Lions with marble fountain, Hall of the Abencerrajes geometric dome, Generalife gardens with water channels, stucco arabesques, muqarnas honeycomb vaulting.

name: Amber Fort (Amer Fort)
description: A fortified palace complex on a hilltop overlooking Maota Lake, blending Hindu and Mughal architectural styles.
historical_significance: Former capital of the Kachwaha Rajputs; UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Hill Forts of Rajasthan, 2013).
architectural_features: Diwan-i-Aam and Diwan-i-Khas, Sheesh Mahal (mirror palace) with thousand tiny mirrors, Ganesh Pol gateway, elephant ascent path, mirror-inlaid ceilings.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Hill Forts of Rajasthan

name: Ancient City of Anuradhapura
description: Ancient capital of Sri Lanka, one of the longest continuously inhabited cities in the world, sacred to Buddhists.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1982); birthplace of Sri Lankan civilization; over 2,500 years of Buddhist history.
architectural_features: Sri Maha Bodhi tree (sacred fig), Ruwanwelisaya stupa 55m high, Jetavanarama stupa once tallest in the world, Abhayagiri monastery complex, sacred precincts with monastic cells.

name: Ancient City of Polonnaruwa
description: Medieval capital with well-preserved ruins of palaces, temples, and statues from the Sinhalese kingdom.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1982); finest example of medieval Sri Lankan urban planning and Buddhist art.
architectural_features: Gal Vihara rock-cut Buddha statues (13m seated, 7m standing), Tooth Relic Temple, Lotus Pond, Alahana Parivena monastery, bronze Buddha statues, ornate stupas.

name: Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus
description: Ancient theatre with exceptionally well-preserved stage building and legendary acoustics, still used for performances today.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); considered the most perfect ancient Greek theatre; attributed to architect Polykleitos the Younger.
architectural_features: Semi-circular orchestra, 55 tiers of marble seats holding 14,000 spectators, symmetrical tier arrangement, excellent acoustics allowing whisper to carry to top row.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Ancient Epidaurus

name: Angkor Thom and Bayon
description: Last capital of the Khmer Empire featuring the famous Bayon temple with its smiling stone faces.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1992); monumental expression of Mahayana Buddhist cosmology.
architectural_features: Bayon temple with 54 towers bearing 216 giant serene faces, four elaborately carved triumphal gates, Terrace of the Elephants, banyan trees growing over ruins.

name: Angkor Wat
description: Largest religious monument in the world, originally Hindu then Buddhist, masterpiece of Khmer architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1992); symbol of Cambodia appearing on its national flag; represents Mount Meru, home of the gods.
architectural_features: Five lotus-bud towers rising 65m, 3km longGallery bas-reliefs depicting Ramayana and Mahabharata, moat 190m wide, galleries with devata carvings, cruciform terraces.

name: Archaeological Areas of Pompeii
description: Ancient Roman city preserved by volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius eruption, offering unmatched insight into daily Roman life.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1997); most complete archaeological record of a Roman city.
architectural_features: Forum with Temple of Jupiter, amphitheatre, thermae (baths), villas with mosaic floors, plaster casts of victims, frescoes and street graffiti.

name: Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere
description: Ancient basilica in the Trastevere district, one of the most beautiful early Christian churches in Rome.
historical_significance: One of Rome's oldest churches; traditionally dated to the 4th century when Pope Urban I built the first chapel.
architectural_features: 12 ancient granite columns supporting a Romanesque nave, golden Byzantine mosaics in the apse depicting the Virgin and Child, campanile, cosmatesque floor.

sources.title: Diocese of Rome - Santa Maria in Trastevere

name: Belém Tower (Torre de Belém)
description: Fortified tower on the Tagus riverbank, iconic symbol of the Portuguese Age of Discovery.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); masterpiece of Manueline architecture; departure point for explorers.
architectural_features: Moorish-inspired merlons, rope motifs in stone, ornate window frames, underground dungeon, armory room, balcony overlooking river, statue of Saint Vincent.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Monument of Belém)

name: Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque)
description: Ottoman imperial mosque known for its blue Iznik tile interior and six minarets, directly facing the Hagia Sophia.
historical_significance: Icon of Istanbul's skyline; considered the last great mosque of the classical Ottoman period.
architectural_features: Six minarets, central dome flanked by four semi-domes, blue Iznik tile work in interior, massive courtyard with ablution fountain, marble pillars.

name: Borobudur Temple
description: Largest Buddhist temple in the world, a massive stepped pyramid covered in 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddha statues.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1991); greatest Buddhist monument in Southeast Asia; represents the cosmos in stone.
architectural_features: Nine stacked platforms (6 square, 3 circular), 72 bell-shaped stupas perforated with Buddha statues, 2,672 narrative relief panels, 504 Buddha statues, mandala ground plan.

name: Boudhanath Stupa
description: One of the largest spherical stupas in Nepal and the world, central pilgrimage site for Tibetan Buddhism.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979, as part of Kathmandu Valley); one of the largest Buddhist monuments in Nepal.
architectural_features: 36m diameter base, white dome with golden spire, all-seeing eyes of Buddha painted on all four sides, conical harmika umbrella, circumambulation path with prayer wheels.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Kathmandu Valley

name: Brandenburg Gate
description: Neoclassical monument marking the site of the former Berlin Wall, symbol of German division and reunification.
historical_significance: Most famous landmark of Germany; symbol of European unity; site of historic moments including WWII liberation and 1989 Wall fall.
architectural_features: Doric hexastyle colonnade, Quadriga bronze chariot atop, 12 columns forming 5 passageways, Elbe sandstone construction, Peace and Victory allegories.

name: Brasília
description: Purpose-built capital city designed by Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa, masterpiece of modernist urban planning.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); first planned capital built in the 20th century; audacious modernist experiment.
architectural_features: Airplane-shaped urban plan, National Congress with twin towers and domes, Cathedral of Brasília with hyperboloid concrete ribs, Palácio da Alvorada, Supreme Court building.

name: Brihadisvara Temple (Big Temple)
description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Shiva, built by Rajaraja Chola I, the first complete grand temple of the Chola dynasty.
historical_significance: Peak of Chola architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987, as Great Living Chola Temples).
architectural_features: Vimana (tower) rising 66 metres topped by a single stone weighing 80 tonnes, 24-hectare temple complex, Nandi pavilion, expansive prakara walls, mural paintings.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Great Living Chola Temples)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Great Living Chola Temples

name: Buckingham Palace
description: London residence and administrative headquarters of the British monarch, symbol of the British monarchy worldwide.
historical_significance: Official royal residence since 1837; site of state occasions and diplomatic receptions; iconic symbol of British sovereignty.
architectural_features: White Portland stone facade, central balustraded terrace, 775 rooms including Ballroom and Long Gallery, garden lake, iron railings and gates.

name: Bulguksa Temple
description: Historic Buddhist temple representing the best of Buddhist art of the early Zen period.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995, with Seokguram); most important Buddhist temple in Korea; symbol of Korean Buddhist art.
architectural_features: Dabotap multi-tiered pagoda with intricate stonework, Tongd Mokchang staircase, Geungnakjeon main hall, bronze Buddha statues, stone lanterns, temple grounds on mountainside.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Monuments of Gyeongju)

name: Canterbury Cathedral
description: One of the oldest and most famous Christian structures in England, seat of the Archbishop of Canterbury.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); center of Christianity in England for 1,400+ years; martyrdom of Thomas Becket in 1170.
architectural_features: Tudor bell tower, Gothic nave with flying buttresses, Trinity Chapel with Becket's tomb, chapter house, cloister gardens, stained glass from 12th century.

name: Centro Historico de Mexico City
description: Historic center built over the Aztec capital Tenochtitlan, containing some of the most important colonial architecture in the Americas.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); largest collection of colonial architecture in the Americas; built atop the destroyed Aztec capital.
architectural_features: Metropolitan Cathedral onAztec temple foundations, National Palace with Rivera murals, Templo Mayor ruins, Palacio de Bellas Artes, Zocalo plaza, Casa de los Azulejos.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Mexico City

name: Changdeokgung Palace
description: Joseon dynasty royal palace harmoniously integrated with the natural landscape of Seoul's secret garden.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1997); finest example of Korean palace architecture; secret garden (Huwon) is a masterpiece of landscape design.
architectural_features: Injeongjeon throne hall with dragon pillar, Donggung pavilion over pond, Biwon (Secret Garden) with ponds and pavilions, traditional Korean roof curves, ondol heating systems.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Royal Palaces of Joseon)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Seoul Palaces

name: Chartres Cathedral
description: Highpoint of French Gothic architecture, famous for its intact medieval stained-glass windows and labyrinth.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); contains 174 original 12th-13th century stained glass windows; major medieval pilgrimage destination.
architectural_features: Twin west towers of different styles, Rose windows with deep blue 'Chartres blue', nave vaulting at 37m, stone labyrinth on floor, pyramidal spires.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Chartres Cathedral

name: Chichen Itza
description: Major pre-Columbian Maya city featuring El Castillo pyramid, Great Ball Court, and Temple of Warriors.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); one of the New Seven Wonders of the World; demonstrates advanced Maya astronomy and engineering.
architectural_features: El Castillo pyramid with 365 steps (solar calendar), serpent shadow phenomenon at equinox, Great Ball Court with acoustics, Temple of Warriors with colonnades, observatory El Caracol.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Chichen Itza

name: Chittor Fort
description: The largest fort in India, perched atop a 180-metre high hill, associated with Rajput valour and sacrifice.
historical_significance: Symbol of Rajput resistance against Mughal invasions; UNESCO World Heritage Site (as part of Hill Forts of Rajasthan, 2013).
architectural_features: Seven successive defensive gates, Kirti Stambha (victory tower), Vijay Stambha (victory tower with nine stories), Rani Ki Vav stepwell, Padmini Palace.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Hill Forts of Rajasthan)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Hill Forts of Rajasthan

name: Christ the Redeemer (Cristo Redentor)
description: Art Deco statue of Jesus Christ with arms outstretched atop Corcovado mountain, most iconic symbol of Brazil.
historical_significance: New Seven Wonder of the World; most recognizable symbol of Christianity and Rio de Janeiro.
architectural_features: 28m tall statue (38m with pedestal), reinforced concrete and soapstone exterior, Art Deco geometric forms, panoramic views of city, tram railway to summit.

name: City Palace, Udaipur
description: A vast palace complex on the banks of Lake Pichola, built by Maharana Udai Singh II, blending Rajput and Mughal styles.
historical_significance: Residence of the Mewar royal family for over 400 years; one of the largest palace complexes in India.
architectural_features: Lakshmi Vilas (bell repository), Manak Chowk courtyard, Phool Mahal (flower hall), Mor Chowk (peacock court), panoramic lake views, intricate mirror work and fresco paintings.

name: Colosseum (Flavian Amphitheatre)
description: Largest ancient amphitheatre ever built, capable of holding 50,000-80,000 spectators for gladiatorial contests and public spectacles.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1980); symbol of Imperial Rome and one of the New Seven Wonders of the World.
architectural_features: Four-storey arcade with Doric, Ionic, and Corinthian orders, elliptical plan 189x156m, hypogeum underground network, velarium sail canopy system.

name: Cultural Landscape of Bali: Subak System
description: Rice terraces managed by the subak water-sharing system, embodying the Hindu philosophy of Tri Hita Karana.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012); living cultural landscape demonstrating sustainable agricultural practice.
architectural_features: Step-cut rice terraces, temple complexes (Pura) at water sources, irrigation channels and weirs, volcanic mountain backdrop, traditional Balinese village layout.

name: Edinburgh Castle
period: 12th century CE (on volcanic rock since 850 CE)
description: Historic fortress dominating Edinburgh's skyline from Castle Rock, seat of Scottish royalty for centuries.
historical_significance: One of most important historic sites in Scotland; contains the Scottish Crown Jewels and Stone of Destiny.
architectural_features: Volcanic crag and tail formation, Great Hall, St Margaret's Chapel (oldest building), Castle guns firing daily, Royal Palace interiors, National War Museum.

name: Eiffel Tower (Tour Eiffel)
description: Iron lattice tower on the Champ de Mars, built as the entrance arch for the 1889 World's Fair.
historical_significance: Most-visited paid monument in the world; symbol of France and engineering achievement of the Industrial Age.
architectural_features: 330m wrought-iron lattice structure, three levels with restaurants, 18,038 metallic components, 2.5 million rivets, four arched legs at base.
heritage_status: Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site (Paris, Banks of the Seine)

name: Elephanta Caves
description: Rock-cut cave temples on Elephanta Island dedicated primarily to Shiva, featuring monumental sculpture.
historical_significance: Masterpieces of Indian sculpture; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); considered among the finest examples of Hindu cave art.
architectural_features: Mahaeshmurti (three-headed Shiva) colossal statue, carved pillared halls, Nandi shrine, intricate bas-reliefs depicting Shiva cosmic dances.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Elephanta Caves

name: Essaouira (Mogador)
description: Coastal fortress city with distinctive Portuguese and Moroccan architecture, historic port on the Atlantic.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2001); well-preserved example of 18th-century North African fortified town.
architectural_features: Skala de la Ville sea fortress with cannon emplacements, medina with fortified ramparts, Portuguese-style grid streets, cedar wood doors, harbor with fishing boats.

name: Fasil Ghebbi, Gondar
description: Royal enclosure of castles and palaces built by Ethiopian emperors, called the 'Camelot of Africa'.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); last major royal compound of the Ethiopian Empire; unique African fortress architecture.
architectural_features: Fasilides' Castle with thick walls and battlements, Debre Birhan Selassie church with ceiling paintings, library with ancient manuscripts, bathhouse of Fasilides, towered gateways.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
description: Abandoned Mughal city built by Emperor Akbar as his capital, now a remarkably preserved example of Mughal urban planning.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); represents Akbar's vision of a multi-religious empire through its architecture.
architectural_features: Buland Darwaza (Gateway of Greatness), Jama Masjid with Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Khas with central pillar, Patthar Mahal, Anguri Bagh, massive city walls.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Fatehpur Sikri

name: Feroz Shah Kotla
description: Fortress built by Feroz Shah Tughlaq, featuring the imposing Ashoka Pillar brought from Meerut.
historical_significance: Important monument of the Tughlaq period; showcases the reuse of ancient pillars in Islamic architecture.
architectural_features: Ashoka Pillar with Brahmi inscriptions, octagonal tomb of Feroz Shah, mosque with arched entrances, reservoir ( Hauz Khas), massive stone walls.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Feroz Shah Kotla

name: Florence Cathedral (Santa Maria del Fiore)
description: Gothic cathedral famous for Brunelleschi's revolutionary dome, the largest masonry dome ever built.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1982); masterpiece of Renaissance engineering and architecture.
architectural_features: Red terracotta dome by Brunelleschi, green-white-pink marble facade, Giotto's Campanile, Baptistery with Gates of Paradise, vast interior.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Centre of Florence)

name: Forbidden City
description: Imperial palace complex in central Beijing, residence of Chinese emperors for nearly 500 years during the Ming and Qing dynasties.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); largest collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in China; symbol of Chinese imperial power.
architectural_features: Nine gates, golden glazed tile roofs, massive courtyards, vermilion walls, dragon-carved marble terraces, double-eave hip roofs, 9999.5 rooms.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Forbidden City

name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
description: Shinto shrine dedicated to Inari, the god of rice and prosperity, famous for its thousands of vermilion torii gates.
historical_significance: Head shrine of all 30,000 Inari shrines in Japan; one of Kyoto's most iconic landmarks.
architectural_features: Senbon Torii (thousands of vermilion gates), fox statues (Inari's messengers), main hall with cypress bark roof, sacred mountain trails, sub-shrines.

name: Gallipoli Peninsula Battlefields
description: Battlefield complex commemorating the WWI Gallipoli Campaign, significant to both Turkey and Australia/New Zealand.
historical_significance: Founding moment of modern Turkey; ANZAC Day originates from this campaign; strategic straits control.
architectural_features: ANZAC Cove landing site, Lone Pine memorial, Chunuk Bair cemetery, Turkish martyrs memorial with crescent finial, naval guns on headlands.

name: Gettysburg National Military Park
description: Site of the decisive Battle of Gettysburg, the turning point of the American Civil War.
historical_significance: Most important Civil War battlefield; site of Lincoln's Gettysburg Address; 50,000+ casualties in three days.
architectural_features: Devil's Den boulders, Little Round Top with rifle trenches, Citadell Avenue with 1,400+ monuments, Soldiers' National Cemetery with Lincoln's tomb, Gettysburg Museum.

name: Grand Canyon National Park
description: Steep-sided canyon carved by the Colorado River, one of the largest and most spectacular canyons in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); natural wonder showcasing 2 billion years of geological history.
architectural_features: 446km long canyon up to 29km wide and 1.8km deep, layered red rock strata, Colorado River at base, viewpoint terraces, ancient petroglyphs.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Grand Canyon

name: Great Pyramid of Giza (Pyramid of Khufu)
description: The oldest and largest of the three pyramids in the Giza pyramid complex, built as a tomb for Pharaoh Khufu.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); only surviving wonder of the Ancient World; original height 146.6m.
architectural_features: Limestone blocks weighing 2.5-15 tonnes each, ascending corridor, King's Chamber with granite sarcophagus, Grand Gallery, external casing stones visible at base.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Ancient Memphis and its Necropolis)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Memphis and its Necropolis

name: Great Sphinx of Giza
description: Limestone statue with a lion's body and human head, facing east towards the rising sun, guarding the Giza plateau.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); largest monolithic statue in the world at 73m long and 20m high.
architectural_features: Carved from bedrock limestone, missing royal beard, ceremonial nose restored, weathering patterns on enclosure walls.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Ancient Memphis and its Necropolis)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Memphis and its Necropolis

name: Great Wall (Badaling Section)
description: Massive stone and brick fortification stretching over 21,000 km, built to protect Chinese states from invasions.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); longest man-made structure in the world; symbol of Chinese resilience and engineering.
architectural_features: Watchtower towers every 100-200 metres, crenellated parapets, beacon towers on ridgelines, stone and brick construction, earthen ramparts.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Great Wall

name: Group of Monuments at Hampi
description: Remnants of the Vijayanagara Empire capital, set in a dramatic landscape of boulders and temples.
historical_significance: One of the largest medieval urban complexes in India; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); once the second-largest city in the world.
architectural_features: Vitthala Temple with stone chariot and musical pillars, Virupaksha Temple gopuram, Queen's Bath, corbelled arches, monumental pillar halls, sacred precincts.

name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
description: Monuments built by the Pallava dynasty featuring rock-cut temples, sculptural reliefs, and structural temples on the Coromandel Coast.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984); showcases the transition from rock-cut to structural temple architecture.
architectural_features: Arjuna's Penance (largest open-air rock relief), Shore Temple with vimana towers, five Rathas (chariot temples), cave temples with giant reliefs of Ganga.

name: Group of Monuments at Pattadakal
description: A cluster of Hindu and Jain temples built in both Nagara and Dravida styles, representing the confluence of North and South Indian temple architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); ceremonial coronation site of the Chalukya dynasty.
architectural_features: Virupaksha Temple with stepped pyramid tower, Papanatha Temple in Nagara style, Galaganatha Temple with rich sculptures, shared mandapa halls.

name: Guggenheim Museum Bilbao
description: Iconic contemporary museum building by Frank Gehry, transformed Bilbao from industrial decline to cultural tourism destination.
historical_significance: Pioneered the 'Bilbao Effect' - using architecture to revitalize cities; titanium-clad curves rival any historic monument.
architectural_features: Titanium and limestone curves, glass atrium spiraling 50m, undulating forms reflecting river light, spiral galleries, urban plaza with 'Puppy' sculpture.

name: Hagia Eirene (Church of Peace)
description: Byzantine church in the Topkapi Palace grounds, one of the few Constantinople churches not converted to a mosque.
historical_significance: Oldest church in Istanbul still standing; used as imperial treasury after Ottoman conquest.
architectural_features: Basilica plan with three naves, massive dome on pendentives, brick construction with stone bands, original marble floor, apse with mosaic fragments.

name: Hagia Sophia
description: Former Eastern Orthodox Catholic patriarchal basilica, later an imperial mosque, now a mosque, showcasing Byzantine and Ottoman architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2014); masterpiece of Byzantine architecture; symbol of Istanbul for 1,500 years.
architectural_features: Massive central dome 31m diameter rising 55m, pendentive support system, marble screens with Islamic calligraphy, minarets added by Ottomans, golden mosaics.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Areas of Istanbul)

name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
description: A five-story pyramidal facade with 953 small windows (jharokhas) built to allow royal women to observe street festivals while remaining unseen.
historical_significance: Iconic symbol of Jaipur; unique architectural response to social customs of purdah.
architectural_features: Honeycomb-like facade with intricate latticework, pyramidal shape, thirteen stories, internal corridors and staircases, red and pink sandstone construction.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Hawa Mahal

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial (Genbaku Dome)
description: Ruined industrial support building left intact by the atomic bomb, preserved as a symbol of nuclear devastation and peace.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1996); most powerful symbol of nuclear destruction and the peace movement.
architectural_features: Dome-shaped skeletal frame rising from ruined concrete base, ribs visible against sky, preserved blast damage, surrounding park with atomic bomb museum.

name: Historic Centre of Bukhara
description: Well-preserved medieval Central Asian city with over 140 architectural monuments spanning 1,000+ years.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993); major center of Islamic culture and trade on the Silk Road; 'the museum of Central Asia'.
architectural_features: Poi-Kalyan complex with Kalyan Minaret (46.5m), Kalyan Mosque, Mir-i-Arab Madrasa, trading domes (coups), Ark Fortress, Ismail Samani Mausoleum (9th century).

name: Historic Centre of Cusco
description: Former capital of the Inca Empire with colonial Spanish architecture built atop Inca foundations.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); capital of the Inca Empire (Tawantinsuyu); living testimony of Andean and Spanish colonial fusion.
architectural_features: Temple of Coricancha with gold-plated walls, San Juan Church built over Inca walls, 12-angled stone in Calle Santa Teresa, Plaza de Armas, baroque facades on Inca foundations.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: Tomb of the Mughal emperor Humayun, built by his wife Hamida Banu Begum. First garden-tomb in the Indian subcontinent.
historical_significance: Precursor to the Taj Mahal; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993); exemplifies Mughal architectural grandeur.
architectural_features: Double dome with pyramidal roof, Charbagh garden layout, red sandstone and white marble inlay, octagonal tomb chamber, eight pishtaq arches.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Humayun's Tomb

name: Iguazu Falls (Cataratas do Iguaçu)
description: Spectacular waterfall system on the Iguazu River, comprising 275 individual falls over 2.7km width.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); one of the seven natural wonders of the world; largest waterfall system by volume.
architectural_features: Devil's Throat (Garganta del Diablo) U-shaped cascade, 150m drop, walkway platforms, subtropical rainforest setting, colorful rainbows in spray.

name: India Gate
description: A 42-metre tall war memorial arch on Kingsway, commemorating 90,000 Indian soldiers killed in World War I and the Third Anglo-Afghan War.
historical_significance: Central landmark of New Delhi; inspired by Rome's Arch of Constantine; Amar Jawan Jyoti flame beneath since 1971.
architectural_features: Sandstone triumphal arch, inscribed names of soldiers, eternal flame memorial, central bowl, bas-relief panels.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture India - India Gate

name: Itchan Kala, Khiva
description: Walled inner city of Khiva, a remarkably preserved example of Central Asian Islamic architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1990); one of the best-preserved medieval cities on the Silk Road.
architectural_features: 4km of mud-brick walls, Islam Khoja Minaret (slenderest in Uzbekistan), Khan Mosque with painted ceiling, Muhammad Amin Khan Madrasa, ornate wooden columns.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Itchan Kala

name: Itmad-ud-Daulah's Tomb (Baby Taj)
description: Tomb of Mirza Ghiyas Beg, considered a dream woven in marble and a precursor to the Taj Mahal.
historical_significance: First Mughal tomb to use pietra dura (gemstone inlay); transitional architecture between Akbar and Shah Jahan periods.
architectural_features: White marble structure with extensive pietra dura floral and calligraphic inlay, chatris (chhatris) on roof, garden setting, delicate jali screens.

name: Itsukushima Shrine (Miyajima)
description: Shinto shrine famous for its 'floating' torii gate in the Seto Inland Sea, appearing to float at high tide.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1996); major pilgrimage site since ancient times; symbol of Japanese aesthetic harmony with nature.
architectural_features: Vermillion torii gate standing in sea, Shinden-zukuri style shrine with connecting corridors, stage-like main hall over water, tidal variations affecting appearance.

name: Jama Masjid, Delhi
description: One of the largest mosques in India, commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan with capacity for 25,000 worshippers.
historical_significance: Last great monument of the Mughal era; reflects Shah Jahan's architectural patronage alongside the Taj Mahal.
architectural_features: Three white marble domes on red sandstone base, two 40-metre minarets, vast courtyard with marble mosque, arched entrances, carved stone screens.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Jama Masjid Delhi

name: Jerónimos Monastery
description: Former Benedictine monastery, finest example of Manueline architecture, burial place of Vasco da Gama and Luís de Camões.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); symbol of Portuguese maritime power; masterpiece of Gothic-Manueline style.
architectural_features: Intricate stone carvings of ropes, spheres, and marine motifs, cloister with ribbed vaults, royal pantheon, twin bell towers, carved walnut doors.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Monument of Belém)

name: Jongmyo Shrine
description: Royal ancestral shrine of the Joseon dynasty, site of Jongmyo Jeryeak ancestral ritual since 1394.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995); oldest royal ancestral shrine in Korea; ritual performed continuously for over 600 years.
architectural_features: Jongmyo Shrine hall with 19 ancestral tablets, hyeonpu stone elephants, vermilion lacquered pillars, traditional music performance pavilion, ceremonial grounds.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Royal Ancestral Rituals and Songs)

name: Kairouan Great Mosque
description: One of the most important mosques in the Islamic world, founded by the Arab general Uqba ibn Nafi.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988, as City of Kairouan); fourth holiest city of Islam; model for later mosques including Al-Azhar and Cordoba.
architectural_features: Square plan with courtyard, 124 columns from Roman ruins, massive wooden doors, tiered minaret, hypostyle prayer hall, sacred pool for ablutions.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (City of Kairouan)

name: Karnak Temple Complex
description: Vast open-air museum and ancient religious complex dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); largest ancient religious site ever built; worshipped for over 2,000 years.
architectural_features: Hypostyle Hall with 134 massive papyrus-column capitals, Great Aten Temple, sacred lake, obelisk of Hatshepsut, processional sphinx avenue.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Thebes: Ancient Capital with its Necropolis)

name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple
description: One of the holiest Hindu temples dedicated to Lord Shiva, located on the banks of the Ganges River in Varanasi.
historical_significance: Central shrine of Hindu pilgrimage; mentioned in ancient scriptures as the abode of Shiva since time immemorial.
architectural_features: Gold-plated spire, marble corridors, intricate carvings, sacred Ganges ghats adjacent, Nandi statue in courtyard.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: A group of Hindu and Jain temples known for their nagara-style architectural symbolism and sculptural decoration.
historical_significance: Peak of North Indian temple architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); built by the Chandela Dynasty.
architectural_features: Shikhara (curvilinear tower) rising from a high platform, intricate erotic and celestial sculptures, mandapa (pillared hall), garbhagriha (sanctum), stepped decorative terraces.

name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
description: Zen Buddhist temple covered in gold leaf, reflecting perfectly in the mirror pond below.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1994); original pavilion built as retirement villa for shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu.
architectural_features: Three-storey pagoda-style building, gold-leaf exterior on upper two floors, pine tree on roof pinnacle, Kyo-chi-chin pond reflection, Rokuson-in garden.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Monuments of Ancient Kyoto)

name: Leaning Tower of Pisa
description: Freestanding bell tower known for its unintended lean caused by soft foundation soil during construction.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987, as part of Piazza dei Miracoli); engineering marvel demonstrating medieval structural ingenuity.
architectural_features: Romanesque marble cylinders, 296 steps, eight storeys of arcades, 54.86m height, 3.97-degree tilt, white Carrara marble exterior.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Piazza del Duomo, Pisa)

name: Loire Valley Chateaux
description: Concentration of historic chateaux along the Loire River, representing the pinnacle of French Renaissance architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2000); cultural landscape showcasing the Renaissance revival of classical ideals in architecture and garden design.
architectural_features: Chateau de Chambord with double-helix staircase, Chateau de Chenonceau spanning the river, Chateau de Amboise with Leonardo's tomb, formal French gardens.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Loire Valley

name: Luxor Temple
description: Ancient Theban temple on the east bank of the Nile, devoted to the rejuvenation of kingship and the god Amun.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); connected to Karnak by a 2.7km Sphinx Avenue used in the Opet Festival.
architectural_features: Colonnaded courts, Great Hypostyle Hall, massive pylon entrance, sacred lake, towering obelisk of Ramses II, colossal statue fragments.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Thebes: Ancient Capital with its Necropolis)

name: Machu Picchu
description: 15th-century Inca citadel set high in the Andes, one of the most iconic archaeological sites in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); New Seven Wonder of the World; lost to Europeans until 1911; masterpiece of Inca engineering.
architectural_features: Terraced slopes following mountain contours, Temple of the Sun with circular walls, Intihuatana stone, Room of the Three Windows, precise ashlar masonry without mortar, urban and agricultural sectors.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Machu Picchu

name: Medina of Fez
description: One of the world's largest car-free urban areas, a labyrinth of medieval alleys, madrasas, and souks.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1981); secondholiest city in Islam; home to the world's oldest university (al-Qarawiyyin, founded 859).
architectural_features: Bou Inania Madrasa with zellij tilework, Al-Attarine Madrasa, Tanneries of Chouara (ancient dye pits), 9th-century city walls, 9,000+ alleyways, ornate wooden doors.

name: Medina of Marrakech
description: Historic walled city famous for its vibrant souks, palaces, and the iconic Djemaa el-Fna square.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985); imperial city showcasing Berber, Arab, and Andalusian architectural traditions.
architectural_features: Koutoubia Mosque with 77m minaret, Bahia Palace with mosaic courtyards, Saadian Tombs with marble screens, Djemaa el-Fna square, intricate riad gardens.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
period: 6th century CE origins; 16th century current structure
description: A historic Hindu temple dedicated to Goddess Meenakshi (Parvati) and Lord Sundareswarar (Shiva), one of the most visited religious sites in India.
historical_significance: One of the oldest functioning temples in India; landmark of Dravidian architecture.
architectural_features: Four towering gopurams covered with thousands of vividly painted sculptures, thousand-pillar hall with carved pillars, sacred tank, intricate gold-finial vimana.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Meenakshi Temple

name: Messilah Temple
description: A historic Hindu temple in Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh.
historical_significance: Local heritage site with historical significance to the region.
architectural_features: Traditional North Indian temple architecture with carved pillars and sanctum.

name: Meteora Monasteries
description: Eastern Orthodox monasteries built atop enormous natural rock pillars in central Greece, among the most spectacular monastic complexes in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); second most important Byzantine monastic center after Mount Athos.
architectural_features: Six large monasteries perched on sandstone columns up to 400m high, fresco-covered churches, stone staircases carved into rock, isolated walkways, defensive walls.

name: Mezquita-Catedral of Cordoba
description: Monumental mosque-cathedral blending Islamic and Christian architecture, once the largest in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984); symbol of convivencia between Muslim and Christian cultures; masterpiece of Moorish architecture.
architectural_features: Forest of double-deck red-and-white arches,Mihrab prayer niche with golden mosaics, Renaissance cathedral nave inserted inside, bell tower from minaret, Courtyard of Orange Trees.

name: Milan Cathedral (Duomo di Milano)
description: Greatest Italian example of Gothic architecture, taking six centuries to complete, with an impressive rooftop terrace.
historical_significance: Largest church in Italy; symbol of Milan and Italian Gothic craftsmanship.
architectural_features: 135 spires and 3,400 statues, pointed arches and flying buttresses, golden Madonnina statue on apex, rose windows, marble facade in pink Verona stone.

name: Mont Saint-Michel
description: Tide-swept island commune crowned by a medieval abbey, one of the most recognizable landmarks in France.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); masterpiece of Gothic architecture; pilgrimage site since 708 CE.
architectural_features: Gothic abbey with flying buttresses, Romanesque crypt, steep cobbled streets, fortified ramparts, tidal flats surrounding the rock, spire with archangel Michael statue.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Mont Saint-Michel

name: Museum Island, Berlin
description: Group of five world-renowned museums on an island in the Spree River, housing collections spanning millennia.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1999); one of the most important museum complexes in the world.
architectural_features: Pergamon Museum with Ishtar Gate and Market Gate, Altes Museum with neoclassical portico, Neues Museum with Nefertiti bust, Bode Museum with baroque dome, Alte Nationalgalerie.

name: Nalanda Mahavihara
description: Remains of one of the world's first great universities, a Buddhist monastic university and center of learning for over 800 years.
historical_significance: Ancient seat of Buddhist learning attracting scholars from across Asia; UNESCO World Heritage Site (2016).
architectural_features: Stupas and viharas (monasteries), temple foundations, terracotta plaques, brick structures with ornamental facades, ancient library ruins.

name: Naqsh-e Jahan Square
description: One of the largest city squares in the world, surrounded by mosques, palaces, and bazaars from the Safavid era.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); masterpiece of Islamic urban design; heart of Safavid Isfahan.
architectural_features: 546m x 160m rectangle, Shah Mosque with seven-color mosaic tiles, Sheikh Lotfollah Mosque with pearlescent dome, Ali Qapu Palace with music room, vast bazaar arcade.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Naqsh-e Jahan Square)

name: Nazca Lines
description: Massive ancient geoglyphs etched into the desert plateau, depicting animals, plants, and geometric shapes visible only from the air.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1994); one of archaeology's greatest mysteries; demonstrates extraordinary precision and planning.
architectural_features: Over 800 straight lines up to 30km long, 300+ geometric figures, animal representations including hummingbird, spider, monkey, 90m condor, 300m lizard, trapezoid shapes.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Nazca Lines

name: Neuschwanstein Castle
description: Romantic hill castle commissioned by King Ludwig II, inspiration for Disney's Sleeping Beauty Castle.
historical_significance: Most visited castle in Germany; symbol of 19th-century Romanticism; influenced castle design worldwide.
architectural_features: Romanesque Revival towers and facades, Swan Knight Hall with murals, throne room with mosaic, marble bathroom with plumbing, Alpine mountain setting.

name: Nikko Toshogu Shrine
description: Opulent Shinto shrine dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu, founder of the Tokugawa shogunate, the most elaborate shrine in Japan.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1999); peak of Edo-period decorative art; most visited shrine in Japan.
architectural_features: Yomeimon Gate with 200 woodcarvings, seven-storied pagoda, ornate tomb with golden decorations, 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys carved in stone.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Shrines and Temples of Nikko)

name: Ouro Preto Historic Town
description: Well-preserved colonial mining town, center of the Brazilian Gold Rush, rich in Baroque art and architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1980); finest example of Brazilian colonial architecture; birthplace of Brazilian independence movement.
architectural_features: Church of Saint Francis of Assisi with Aleijadinho sculptures, Santo Ildefonso church with gold leaf interior, cobblestone streets, stepped terrain, baroque cathedrals.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Ouro Preto

name: Palace of Knossos
description: Largest Bronze Age archaeological site on Crete and regarded as Europe's oldest city, legendary home of King Minos and the Labyrinth.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987, as part of Mycenae and Tiryns - extended to include Knossos); heart of Minoan civilization.
architectural_features: Multi-story palace complex with drainage systems, vibrant fresco paintings of bull-leaping, Megaron throne room, central courtyard, storage magazines with giant pithoi jars.

name: Palace of Versailles
description: Royal château and capital of the French monarchy from Louis XIV to the French Revolution, one of the grandest palaces in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); seat of absolute monarchy; signed the Treaty of Versailles ending WWI in the Hall of Mirrors.
architectural_features: Hall of Mirrors with 357 mirrors, Royal Chapel with twin towers, Gardens by Le Notre with 150 fountains, marble courtyards, Queen's Hamlet.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Palace of Versailles

name: Palatine Hill (Palatino)
description: Central hill of the Seven Hills of Rome, site of early Roman settlements and imperial palaces.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1980); legendary birthplace of Rome where Romulus founded the city; residence of emperors.
architectural_features: Domus Augustana and Domus Flavia ruins, Gardens of Farnesina, Vitellian stairs, remains of Nero's golden house, ancient road Via Sacra at base.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Centre of Rome)

name: Palenque
description: Maya city renowned for its sophisticated architecture and intricate stucco reliefs, set in tropical jungle.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); peak of Classic Maya art and architecture; birthplace of King Pakal the Great.
architectural_features: Temple of Inscriptions with Pakal's tomb, Palace complex with distinctive tower, Group of the Crosses temples, refined stucco facades, natural spring integration.

name: Pamukkale Hot Springs
description: White travertine terraces formed by thermal waters, site of ancient Hierapolis spa city.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); natural wonder combined with ancient Greco-Roman spa complex.
architectural_features: Cotton-colored calcium carbonate terraces, Ancient theatre with marble seating, Gate of Apollo, necropolis extending 1km, thermal pools.

name: Pantheon
description: Former Roman temple now a Catholic church, renowned for its massive unreinforced concrete dome with central oculus.
historical_significance: Best-preserved ancient Roman building; influenced Renaissance and Neoclassical architecture worldwide.
architectural_features: 43.3m diameter unreinforced concrete dome, 8m oculus opening, coffered ceiling panels, portico with 8 Corinthian columns, granite interior columns.
heritage_status: Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Centre of Rome)

name: Pantheon, Paris
description: Neoclassical monument in the Latin Quarter, originally a church dedicated to St Genevieve, now a mausoleum for distinguished French citizens.
historical_significance: Final resting place of Voltaire, Rousseau, Hugo, Zola, and Curie; symbol of French secularism and republican values.
architectural_features: Greek-cross plan with massive Corinthian portico, 83m dome with coffered interior, Foucault's pendulum suspension point, oculus with bronze grating.

name: Parthenon
description: Former temple to the goddess Athena, crowning the Acropolis of Athens and the defining symbol of Classical Greece and Western civilization.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); greatest monument of Classical Greece; epitome of Doric architecture.
architectural_features: Octastyle peripteral Doric temple, 8x17 column arrangement, subtle entasis curves, pedimental sculptures, contiguous Ionic frieze, marble construction.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Acropolis of Athens)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Acropolis of Athens

name: Pasargadae
description: First capital of the Achaemenid Empire, containing the tomb of Cyrus the Great.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2004); birthplace of Persian imperial civilization; Cyrus Cylinder is considered first charter of human rights.
architectural_features: Tomb of Cyrus with simple rectangular form and gabled roof, Garden of Cyrus with four-fold water channels, Audience Hall ruins, fortification walls, inscribed stone blocks.

name: Pashupatinath Temple
description: Sacred Hindu temple complex dedicated to Lord Pashupati (Shiva) on the banks of the Bagmati River.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); most sacred Shiva temple in Nepal; important pilgrimage site for Hindus worldwide.
architectural_features: Golden roof and silver doors, four-faced Pashupati statue, ritual cremation ghats, numerous smaller shrines, bell tower, sacred bulls (Nandi), priests in traditional dress.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Kathmandu Valley

name: Persepolis (Takht-e Jamshid)
description: Ceremonial capital of the Achaemenid Empire, founded by Darius the Great, destroyed by Alexander the Great.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); greatest achievement of ancient Persian architecture; symbol of Iranian imperial glory.
architectural_features: Apadana palace with 72 columns, Gate of All Nations, Throne Hall with 100 columns, relief sculptures of 23 subject nations, twin bull-headed columns, massive stairway reliefs.

name: Petra
description: Ancient Nabataean city carved into rose-red sandstone cliffs, famous for its facade known as Al-Khazneh.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985); New Seven Wonder of the World; lost to the Western world until 1812.
architectural_features: Al-Khazneh (Treasury) 40m facade, Al-Deir (Monastery) larger facade, Siq canyon entrance, Royal Tombs with colonnaded facades, Roman-style theater, hypogeum tombs.

name: Porto Historic Centre
description: Medieval city on the Douro river, famous for Port wine cellars and the iconic Dom Luis I Bridge.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1996); one of Europe's oldest cities; birthplace of Port wine trade.
architectural_features: Livraria Lello bookstore with Neo-Gothic interior, São Bento Station with tile panels, Sé Cathedral fortress, Clérigos Tower, Dom Luis I iron bridge, Ribeira waterfront.

name: Potala Palace
description: Massive palace fortress on Red Hill in Lhasa, former residence of the Dalai Lamas and spiritual center of Tibetan Buddhism.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1994); highest and largest ancient fortress in the world at 3,700m altitude.
architectural_features: White and Red Palaces, 13-storey main tower, golden roofs, mural paintings covering 250,000 sq metres, stupas of past Dalai Lamas.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Potala Palace

name: Prambanan Temple Compound
description: Largest Hindu temple complex in Indonesia, dedicated to the Trimurti (Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva).
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1991); masterpiece of Hindu architecture in Southeast Asia; contemporary of Borobudur.
architectural_features: Main temple 47m tall surrounded by 224 smaller temples, bas-relief panels depicting Ramayana, Nandi and Garuda statues, ornate candi (temple) towers, intricately carved lintels.

name: Preah Khan Temple
description: Large temple-complex built by King Jayavarman VII as a memorial to his father, combining Buddhist and Hindu elements.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1992); represents the height of Khmer temple construction under the Bayon style.
architectural_features: Long gallery with elephant capitals, jade terrace, central sanctuary with Buddha image, jungle-entangled ruins, elaborate devata carvings, moat with naga balustrades.

name: Qumran Caves (Dead Sea Scrolls)
description: Caves where the Dead Sea Scrolls were discovered in 1947, profoundly impacting biblical scholarship.
historical_significance: One of the most important archaeological discoveries of the 20th century; Essene settlement where scrolls were hidden.
architectural_features: Eleven cave systems, plastered micro-writes, pottery jars, ancient water cisterns, ritual baths (mikva'ot), community buildings.

name: Qutb Minar and Monuments
description: A 72.5 metre tall red sandstone minaret with intricately carved fluted shaft, the tallest brick minaret in the world.
historical_significance: First Islamic monument in India; commemorates the Delhi Sultanate establishment; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1993).
architectural_features: Fluted tapering tower, three balconies supported by muqarnas brackets, inscriptions in Kufic script, iron pillar with rust-resistant metallurgy, Alai Darwaza gateway.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Qutb Minar

name: Ranganathaswamy Temple, Srirangam
period: 7th century CE origins; 14th century current gopurams
description: One of the largest and oldest functioning Hindu temples in the world, dedicated to Lord Ranganatha (Vishnu resting on the serpent Adishesha).
historical_significance: Most important Vaishnava temple in South India; one of the twelve sacred Abodes of Vishnu.
architectural_features: Seven concentric rectangular walls with ten gopurams, the tallest reaching 73 metres, sacred pond, intricate pillared halls.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Srirangam Temple

name: Red Fort Complex (Lal Qila)
description: Historic fortified palace complex in Old Delhi that served as the main residence of Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years.
historical_significance: Peak of Mughal architecture under Shah Jahan; UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007); site of India's annual Independence Day ceremony.
architectural_features: Red sandstone walls, Diwan-i-Aam (public audience hall), Diwan-i-Khas (private audience hall), Moti Masjid (pearl mosque), Nagina Masjid, luxurious courtyard gardens.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Red Fort Complex

name: Registan Square, Samarkand
description: Iconic square flanked by three magnificent Islamic madrasas, jewel of the Silk Road.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2001, as part of Samarkand); heart of Timurid Renaissance; described by Marco Polo.
architectural_features: Ulugh Beg Madrasa with blue tilework, Tilla-Kori Madrasa with gold facade, Sher-Dor Madrasa with tiger motifs, massive pishtaq arches, muqarnas decoration, central pool.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Samarkand - Crossroads of Cultures)

name: Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras
description: Ancient irrigation system carving terraces into mountain slopes, still actively farmed by indigenous communities.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995); living cultural landscape demonstrating sustainable mountain agriculture for millennia.
architectural_features: Step-cut terraces following mountain contours, ancient渠水 (irrigation) channels, stone walls, Batad and Banaue terraces, indigenous Ifugao villages.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Rice Terraces

name: Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
description: Eleven medieval monolithic rock-cut churches carved downward from single blocks of granite, known as 'New Jerusalem'.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1978); living religious site still used for worship; extraordinary achievement in sacred architecture.
architectural_features: Church of St. George (cross-shaped), Ta Giyorgis with surrounding trench, Bet Golgotha with Solomon's tomb, deep trenches separating churches, narrow passageways, Ethiopian Orthodox crosses.

name: Royal Palace of Madrid (Palacio Real)
description: Largest royal palace in Western Europe, official residence of the Spanish royal family (used for state ceremonies only).
historical_significance: Largest operating royal palace in Europe by floor area; symbol of Spanish Bourbon monarchy.
architectural_features: Baroque-Classicist facade with 3,000 rooms, Royal Armory with historic weapons, Throne Room with Murillo painting, Sabatini Gardens, celestial dome ceiling.

name: Sacsayhuaman Fortress
description: Massive Inca fortress overlooking Cusco with some of the largest stones ever used in construction.
historical_significance: Part of UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); demonstrates Inca military engineering and monumental stonework.
architectural_features: Zigzag walls with stones up to 120 tonnes, perfectly fitted polygonal masonry without mortar, three terraced walls, ceremonial platforms, underground tunnels.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu)

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Machu Picchu

name: Sagarmatha National Park (Everest)
description: Mountain park encompassing Mount Everest (Sagarmatha) and surrounding peaks, the highest point on Earth.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); home to the world's highest peak at 8,848.86m; sacred to Sherpa people.
architectural_features: Khumbu Glacier, Tengboche Monastery, Namche Bazaar, Hillary Step, South Col route, prayer flags and chortens along trails.

name: Sagrada Familia
description: Antoni Gaudi's unfinished masterpiece, the largest unfinished Catholic church in the world, iconic symbol of Barcelona.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2005); Gaudi's life work spanning 43 years; unique synthesis of Gothic and Art Nouveau forms.
architectural_features: Three elaborate facades (Nativity, Passion, Glory), 18 spires representing biblical figures, forest-like interior columns, stained glass creating rainbow light, intricate stone carvings.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Works of Gaudi

name: Sanchi Stupa Complex
description: One of the oldest stone structures in India, a Buddhist complex centered on a hemispherical dome marking relics of the Buddha.
historical_significance: Commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1989); best-preserved ancient Buddhist monument.
architectural_features: Great Stupa with four carved toranas (gateways) depicting Jataka tales, smaller stupas, votive pillars, monastic quadrangles, exquisitely carved gateway reliefs.

name: Sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi
description: Ancient sanctuary dedicated to Apollo, home of the famous Oracle of Delphi, considered the navel (omphalos) of the ancient world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); most important sanctuary of ancient Greece; consulted by rulers and city-states for centuries.
architectural_features: Temple of Apollo with Doric columns, Tholos of circular design, stadium for athletic games, Treasury buildings of city-states, sacred spring, amphitheatre.

name: Sangiran Early Human Site
description: One of the most important early human fossil sites in the world, yielding remains of Java Man.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1996); key evidence for human evolution in Southeast Asia.
architectural_features: Erosion valleys exposing sedimentary layers, fossil-bearing strata, museum with 140+ hominin specimens, excavation sites across 65 sq km.

name: Santiago de Compostela Cathedral
description: Roman Catholic cathedral and endpoint of the Camino de Santiago pilgrimage route, reputed burial site of Saint James.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985); one of Christianity's three great pilgrimage sites alongside Rome and Jerusalem.
architectural_features: Baroque Facade of Glory, Pantleon (rose window), Plateresque cloister, silver censer Botafumeiro swinging at 68 km/h, Romanesque porticoes with sculpted figures.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Santiago de Compostela

name: Seokguram Grotto
description: Artificial granite cave temple housing a magnificent seated Buddha statue, considered a masterpiece of Buddhist art.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1995); 'the most perfect Buddhist sculpture in the world'; architectural and sculptural masterpiece.
architectural_features: Granite dome ceiling with lotus motif, 3.3m seated Buddha with ushnisha, 29 bodhisattvas and guardians in niches, corbel-vaulted construction, atmospheric lighting.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Monuments of Gyeongju)

name: Sforza Castle (Castello Sforzesco)
description: Large fortified castle in the heart of Milan, originally built by the Visconti family and later expanded by the Sforzas.
historical_significance: One of the largest citadels in Europe; symbol of Milanese power during the Renaissance.
architectural_features: Five massive corner towers, 400m perimeter walls, Courtyard of Honor, unfinished fresco by Bramante, Michelangelo's final Pietà fragment, medieval armory.

name: Shah-i-Zinda Necropolis
description: Sacred necropolis with a row of ornate mausoleums adorned with brilliant turquoise tilework.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2001); pilgrimage site dedicated to Kusam ibn Abbas; finest example of Timurid funerary architecture.
architectural_features: Ornate mausoleums with carved stone screens, turquoise and cobalt tile mosaics, arched iwans, geometric patterns, portal decorations, reflecting pools.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Samarkand - Crossroads of Cultures)

name: Shushtar Historical Hydraulic System
description: Ancient system of dams, canals, and water mills demonstrating sophisticated hydraulic engineering.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2009); most impressive hydraulic system of ancient Iran; influenced Roman engineering.
architectural_features: Band-e Kaisar Roman-era dam, 17 water mills, tunnels cutting through rock, diversion weirs, channels and reservoirs, Qanats (underground aqueducts).

name: Sigiriya (Lion Rock)
description: Ancient rock fortress crowned by a palace complex, rising 200m above the surrounding plain.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1982); one of the most impressive ancient fortifications in the world; famous for its frescoes and mirror wall.
architectural_features: Colossal lion paws (now ruined) at entrance, ancient gardens with water features, frescoes of celestial maidens, mirror wall with ancient graffiti, panoramic views from summit, hydraulic systems.

name: Simien Mountains National Park
description: Dramatic mountain landscape with jagged peaks, deep valleys, and endemic wildlife including Gelada baboons.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1978); most spectacular mountain range in Africa; contains Ras Dashen at 4,550m.
architectural_features: Sheika Gena escarpment dropping 1,500m, sharp peaks and seracs, ancient lava flows, endemic species habitat, rock-hewn churches in surrounding area.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Simien Mountains

name: Statue of Liberty
description: Colossal neoclassical sculpture on Liberty Island, a gift from France symbolizing freedom and democracy.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984); iconic symbol of America and welcome to millions of immigrants.
architectural_features: Copper skin (now green patina) over iron framework, tablet inscribed JULY IV MDCCLXXVI, seven-spiked crown representing seven seas/continents, broken chains at feet, torch held aloft.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Statue of Liberty

name: Stone Forest (Shilin)
description: Dramatic limestone karst formations rising up to 40 metres, created by millions of years of erosion.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2007); one of the most spectacular karst formations in the world.
architectural_features: Towering limestone pillars, forest-like formations, natural bridges, underground cave systems, Sword Peak Ridge walkway.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - South China Karst

name: Stonehenge
description: Prehistoric stone circle monument consisting of massive standing stones arranged in a circular setting.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986); most famous prehistoric monument in the world; aligns with summer solstice sunrise.
architectural_features: Sarsen stones up to 7m tall weighing 25-50 tonnes, bluestones from Wales, trilithon horseshoes, heel stone, ancient earthwork enclosure.

name: Summer Palace
description: Vast ensemble of lakes, gardens and palaces in Beijing, serving as an imperial retreat since the Jin dynasty.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1998); masterpiece of Chinese landscape garden design.
architectural_features: Kunming Lake, Longevity Hill, Marble Bridge, Tower of Buddhist Incense, 7-km Long Corridor with painted beams, 17-arch bridge.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Summer Palace

name: Sun Temple, Konark
description: A 13th-century Hindu temple dedicated to the sun god Surya, designed as a colossal stone chariot with twelve carved wheels.
historical_significance: Pinnacle of Kalinga architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984); represents one of the largest temple structures ever built.
architectural_features: Chariot-shaped base, twelve pairs of elaborately carved stone wheels pulled by horses, Jagmohana (assembly hall), remnants of the Natmandir, detailed erotic and mythological sculptures.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Sun Temple Konark

name: Sun Temple, Modhera
description: A Hindu temple dedicated to the sun god Surya, aligned so that first rays illuminate the inner sanctum on spring and summer equinoxes.
historical_significance: Exquisite example of Solanki architecture; known for its elaborate sculptural decoration and innovative orientation.
architectural_features: Surya Kund stepped reservoir, matha (temple hall) with carved pillars, exquisitely carved walls depicting daily life and mythology, ornate doorway with decorative arch.

sources.title: Archaeological Survey of India - Modhera Sun Temple

name: Taj Mahal
description: White marble mausoleum commissioned by Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
historical_significance: Pinnacle of Mughal architecture; UNESCO World Heritage Site (1983); symbol of love recognized globally.
architectural_features: Symmetrical charbagh garden, central onion dome flanked by four smaller domes, four minarets at corners, white marble Pietra Dura inlay work, reflective water channels.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Taj Mahal

name: Temple of Heaven
description: Complex of religious buildings where emperors of the Ming and Qing dynasties made annual sacrifices to heaven.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1998); finest surviving example of Chinese sacrificial architecture.
architectural_features: Hall of Prayer for Good Harvests with three-tiered circular roof, Imperial Vault of Heaven, Echo Wall, Circular Mound Altar with blue marble tiles.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Temple of Heaven

name: Teotihuacan
description: Ancient Mesoamerican city with the largest pyramids in the pre-Columbian Americas, once home to 200,000 people.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); one of the largest ancient cities in the world; influences Aztec cosmology.
architectural_features: Pyramid of the Sun (65m high), Pyramid of the Moon, Avenue of the Dead 4km long, Temple of Quetzalcoatl with carved serpents, Palace of Quetzalpapalotl, extensive mural paintings.

name: Terracotta Army of Qin Shi Huang
description: Thousands of life-sized terracotta sculptures depicting the armies of Qin Shi Huang, China's first emperor, buried with him.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); one of the greatest archaeological discoveries of the 20th century.
architectural_features: Over 8,000 unique soldier figures, bronze chariots, real-size weapons, pits arranged in military formation, individually carved facial features.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor

name: Todai-ji Temple
description: Buddhist temple housing the world's largest bronze statue of Buddha (Daibutsu) in a massive wooden hall.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1998); head temple of Japanese Kegon school of Buddhism; symbol of Nara period cultural zenith.
architectural_features: Great Buddha Hall (Daibutsuden) 57m x 50m, 15m bronze Buddha statue with lotus throne, Nandaimon gate with guardian kings, giant bronze lily cup.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Monuments of Ancient Nara)

name: Tower of London
description: Historic castle on the north bank of the Thames, founded by William the Conqueror, used as palace, prison, armory, and zoo.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1988); 900-year history of power, imprisonment, and execution; houses the Crown Jewels.
architectural_features: White Tower with corner towers, inner and outer wards, Bloody Tower, Traitor's Gate water entrance, medieval armory displays, ravens keeping tradition.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Tower of London

name: Troy (Hisarlik)
description: Legendary city of the Trojan War, excavated by Heinrich Schliemann, one of the most important archaeological sites in the world.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1998); subject of Homer's Iliad; evidence of 9 layers of civilization.
architectural_features: Circular tower (Scheil Tower), defensive walls with gate openings, multi-layered ruins showing successive cities, wooden reconstruction of Trojan Horse gate.

name: Tughlaqabad Fort
description: Ruined fort built by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq, the first ruler of the Tughlaq dynasty, known for its massive walls and strategic location.
historical_significance: Demonstrates military architecture of the early Delhi Sultanate; notable for its massive ramparts and commanding position.
architectural_features: Rubble masonry walls, irregular bastions, narrow winding passages, ruined gateways, watchtowers, austere defensive design.

name: Umm ar-Rasas (Kastrom Mefa'a)
description: Ancient city with well-preserved Byzantine mosaics depicting towns and landscapes of the Holy Land.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2011); important Christian pilgrimage site with exceptional mosaic floor.
architectural_features: Mosaic floor with Greek inscriptions and topographical maps, St. Stephen's Church ruins, tower foundations, early Christian basilicas, Roman road remnants.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Umm ar-Rasas

name: Valley of the Kings
description: Burial place of ancient Egyptian pharaohs, containing over 60 tombs including that of Tutankhamun.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1979); richest archaeological find in modern history with Tutankhamun's tomb.
architectural_features: Decorated burial chambers with vivid wall paintings, descending corridors carved through limestone, anthropoid sarcophagi, papyrus-shaped columns.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Thebes: Ancient Capital with its Necropolis)

name: Venice and its Lagoon
description: City built on 118 small islands connected by 400+ bridges, famous for its canals, Gothic-Renaissance architecture, and maritime history.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); unique urban ecosystem and masterpiece of human creative genius.
architectural_features: St Mark's Basilica with Byzantine domes and golden mosaics, Doge's Palace with Gothic tracery, Rialto Bridge, Grand Canal waterfront palazzi.

name: Vigan Historic Town
description: Best-preserved Spanish colonial town in Asia, showcasing the blend of Southeast Asian and European architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1999); finest example of planned Spanish colonial town in Asia.
architectural_features: Calle Crisologo cobblestone street, ancestral houses with capiz shell windows, bell towers, Bantay Church, Chinese-Inca-Iberian fusion architecture, firewalls.

name: Wadi Rum Protected Area
description: Vast sandstone desert valley with towering red dunes and ancient Nabataean petroglyphs.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2011); 'Valley of the Moon'; filming location for Lawrence of Arabia and The Martian.
architectural_features: Jabal Umm al-Biyara rock arch, Kandara valley petroglyphs, Nabataean inscriptions and altars, ancient water channels, Bedouin tent camps.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Wadi Rum

name: Westminster Abbey
period: 960 CE origins; 1245-1517 CE current Gothic structure
description: Gothic abbey church where coronations, weddings, and burials of British monarchs have taken place for nearly 1,000 years.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); site of every coronation since 1066; Poets' Corner honors literary giants.
architectural_features: Rayonnant Gothic facade with twin towers, Henry VII Chapel with fan vaulting, Norman crypt, rose windows, stone screen choir stalls, tombs of kings and queens.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage List - Westminster Abbey

name: Worms Cathedral (Wormser Dom)
description: Imperial cathedral and burial place of Emperor Henry IV, important Romanesque monument.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2021, as part of Medieval Routes of Santiago de Compostela in Germany); key stop on the pilgrimage route.
architectural_features: Twin west towers with bulbous domes, Romanesque nave with pointed arches, Gothic choir additions, tomb of Emperor Henry IV, vibrant frescoes.

name: Xochimilco Canals
description: Remnants of the ancient Aztec chinampa agricultural system, now a network of canals and floating gardens.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1987); last remaining vestige of the ancient lake and canal system of Tenochtitlan.
architectural_features: Artificial chinampa islands, trajineras (colorful boats), ceramic tile pavilions, floating markets, aqueduct ruins, traditional farming techniques still practiced.

name: Yazd Historic City
description: Desert city with mud-brick architecture adapted to extreme climate, continuous human settlement for 3,000 years.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (2010); finest example of desert city architecture; Zoroastrian community still preserves ancient traditions.
architectural_features: Windcatcher towers (badgirs) for passive cooling, mud-brick alleyways, Jameh Mosque with tallest brick minaret, Fatemi House, Zoroastrian Fire Temple with eternal flame.

name: Yellow Crane Tower
description: Iconic five-storey pavilion on Snake Hill overlooking the Yangtze River, celebrated in classical Chinese poetry for 1,700 years.
historical_significance: Most reproduced subject in Chinese poetry; symbol of Wuhan and southern China.
architectural_features: Five-storey hexagonal pavilion with yellow glazed tiles, upturned eaves, intricate bracket sets, panoramic river views, adjacent pavilions and gardens.

name: Évora Cathedral
description: Massive Gothic cathedral with fortress-like appearance, one of the finest examples of Portuguese Gothic architecture.
historical_significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site (1986, as Historic Centre of Évora); important religious and military monument.
architectural_features: Bastion-like facade with round buttresses, Gothic cloister with azulejo tiles, Royal Pantheon with circular vault, chapel of bones (Capela dos Ossos), bell tower.
heritage_status: UNESCO World Heritage Site (Historic Centre of Évora)
